extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers and readers of Nature Communications (scientific authors and reviewers considering transparent peer review)
extracted.subtask_description: Policy describing Nature Communications' trial of publishing peer review histories for papers submitted from January 2016, including what is published, what remains confidential, how identities are handled, and how the trial will be evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author opt-out / default publication of peer review history
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of papers submitted from January 2016 will be given the option to publish the peer review history of their paper; the journal states it 'will be publishing all reviewer comments to authors and author rebuttal letters for published papers submitted from January 2016, unless the authors ask us not to.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon acceptance authors will be asked whether they agree to the publication of the peer review file along with the accepted version of the manuscript. The trial's success will be evaluated by monitoring parameters such as author opt-out rates; a report is planned within a year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of published peer review files
rubrics_metrics.description: These files will only contain the peer review history at Nature Communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a manuscript is submitted to Nature Communications after review at another Nature journal, those referee reports and author rebuttal letters will remain confidential because they were submitted without prior consent to be published. Published files will focus on reviewer comments to authors and the authors’ responses to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded materials from peer review files
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence between authors and editors, reviewer comments only to the editors, as well as the internal discussions between editors will remain confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy aims to strike a balance between making the information that led to the decision freely available and enabling reviewers, authors and editors to communicate frankly and privately where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity and identity release
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review identities will only be released if a reviewer explicitly agrees to this, for example by signing the comments made to the authors with their name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apart from such circumstances (explicit reviewer consent), the journal will continue to honour reviewer anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial additions to peer review documents
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where not all of the circumstances that lead to an editorial decision on a manuscript are fully captured in peer review files, editorial comments may be added to the peer review document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such editorial comments are intended to ensure the decision rationale is adequately captured alongside reviewer reports and author responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The ultimate decision whether to publish a paper lies with the editors, and is always taken after careful consideration of all arguments raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent peer review does not change that editorial judgment; published peer review material informs readership but does not replace editorial decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access licensing and archive availability
rubrics_metrics.description: From January all new papers will be published with a Creative Commons open access licence, and all subscription-based content from our archive will be made free to read and is available for non-commerical text and data mining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The peer review transparency move coincides with the journal's transformation to full open access (CC BY), intended to enhance accessibility and support text/data mining (non-commercial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and expected benefits of publishing peer review files
rubrics_metrics.description: By enabling the publication of these peer review documents, we take a step towards opening up our editorial decision-making process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal expects publication of reviewer reports to contribute to scientific appreciation of papers, give more credit to reviewers (their assessments will reach a larger audience), and support understanding and accessibility of published papers.
